title: HPLC and spectrophotometry methods for measuring melamine migration from melamine dishes to food simulants
author: Haghi, Shakoori, et al.
materials: The melamine standard solution was used to prepare a serial dilution of 12 different concentrations (0. 5 to 10 μg/ ml) and draw the calibration curve. The solution of deionized distilled water and ethanol (30:70) was used as the mobile phase to be injected into the HPLC column. At first, a 30-min pilot injection was administered to determine the accurate retention times. Afterwards, 10 different melamine concentrations along with deionized distilled water were injected in triplicate to prepare the calibration curve using MS Excel 2013.
Initially, the stock solutions (6.3 μg/ml) for each of melamine and Uranin were prepared. Pure formaldehyde was used as another component of the mentioned complex [3].

Ten different concentrations (0.05 to 2 μg/ml) were prepared from the melamine stock solution. For developing the complex, 0.5 ml Uranin (as the ketone) and l ml formaldehyde were added. Then deionized distilled water was added to reach the 5 ml volume (Table 1). The final Uranin concentration was 0.63 μg/ml, and the final melamine concentrations varied from 0.063 to 2.52 μg/ml. After this, the calibration curve was drawn by reading the absorptions at 210 nm by spectrophotometry. steps.title: Obtain melamine dishes
steps.instruction: Purchase melamine food‑service dishes from five different brands available on the Iranian market.

steps.title: Prepare HPLC calibration standards
steps.instruction: Make a melamine stock solution and prepare a serial dilution of twelve concentrations ranging from 0.5 µg ml⁻¹ to 10 µg ml⁻¹; use deionized distilled water : ethanol (30 : 70, v/v) as the mobile phase, run a 30‑min pilot injection to locate retention times, then inject the ten selected concentrations in triplicate and record the peak areas to construct the calibration curve in MS Excel 2013.

substeps.instruction: Prepare melamine stock solution (concentration not specified, but sufficient for 0.5–10 µg ml⁻¹ dilutions).
Create twelve serial dilutions (0.5, 0.6, … 10 µg ml⁻¹).
Mix mobile phase: deionized distilled water + ethanol 30 : 70 (v/v).
Run a 30‑min pilot HPLC injection to determine melamine retention time.
Inject ten calibration concentrations (selected from the twelve) in triplicate.
Export peak areas to MS Excel 2013 and draw the calibration curve.

steps.title: Validate HPLC method
steps.instruction: Assess linearity, accuracy and precision of the HPLC method according to ICH guidelines using the specified melamine concentrations and replication scheme.

substeps.instruction: Linearity: prepare six standards (0.5, 1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10 µg ml⁻¹) and inject each in triplicate.
Accuracy & precision: prepare three levels (1, 2.5, 10 µg ml⁻¹) from the stock solution.
Perform three replicate injections per day for three consecutive days (total nine injections per level).
Calculate % recovery = (measured – accepted)/accepted × 100.
Record LOD, LOQ, correlation coefficient, slope, intercept, %RSD as required.

steps.title: Prepare spectrophotometric calibration standards
steps.instruction: Generate melamine‑Uranin‑formaldehyde (MUF) complexes covering 0.063–2.52 µg ml⁻¹ melamine and use them to build a calibration curve at 210 nm.

substeps.instruction: Prepare stock solutions of melamine (6.3 µg ml⁻¹) and Uranin (6.3 µg ml⁻¹).
Prepare pure formaldehyde as the third reagent.
From the melamine stock, make ten concentrations ranging from 0.05 µg ml⁻¹ to 2 µg ml⁻¹.
For each concentration add 0.5 ml Uranin and 1 ml formaldehyde, then add deionized distilled water to bring the total volume to 5 ml.
Resulting final concentrations: Uranin = 0.63 µg ml⁻¹; melamine = 0.063–2.52 µg ml⁻¹.
Measure absorbance of each solution at 210 nm (spectrophotometer) and repeat the measurement three times per concentration.
Use the absorbance data to plot the calibration curve (y = 0.0002x – 0.0045, R² = 0.9989).

steps.title: Validate spectrophotometric method
steps.instruction: Confirm the performance of the MUF‑based spectrophotometric assay using the parameters listed in Table 3.

substeps.instruction: Maximum absorption wavelength: 210 nm.
Accuracy (recovery): 95.3 %.
Precision (RSD): 96.2 %.
Slope: 0.0002 abs · ml · µg⁻¹; Intercept: –0.0045.
Linearity range: 63–2520 ng ml⁻¹.
Standard equation: y = 0.0002x – 0.0045.
Correlation coefficient: R² = 0.9989.
Standard error of intercept: 0.004038571; SD of intercept: 0.012115713.

steps.title: Conduct melamine migration experiment
steps.instruction: Expose the melamine dishes to the chosen food simulants under controlled temperature and time, then collect the simulant for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Wash each melamine bowl thoroughly with distilled water and dry in an oven at 30 °C.
Fill each bowl with the simulant (either distilled water or 3 % acetic acid) up to 1 cm from the rim.
Place the bowls in a pre‑heated oven and raise the temperature to 90 °C; maintain this temperature for 90 min to allow migration.
After 90 min, remove the simulant, transfer it into clean glass tubes, and store the tubes in a refrigerator (4 °C) until further processing.

steps.title: Prepare HPLC sample extracts
steps.instruction: Extract melamine from the collected simulant and ready the extract for HPLC injection.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 1 ml of the refrigerated simulant into a capped test tube.
Add 9 ml acetonitrile.
Dry the mixture under a nitrogen stream at 25 °C until completely evaporated.
Reconstitute the residue with 1 ml of the HPLC mobile phase (water : ethanol 30 : 70).
Vortex (full shake) to ensure mixing.
Transfer the solution to an HPLC vial.

steps.title: Inject HPLC samples
steps.instruction: Run the prepared extracts on the HPLC system using the specified chromatographic conditions.

substeps.instruction: Set flow rate to 1 ml min⁻¹.
Set injection volume to 100 µl.
Detect at 220 nm wavelength.
Use the same mobile phase (water : ethanol 30 : 70).
Expect melamine retention time of approximately 6 min.
Record peak areas and calculate melamine concentration using the HPLC calibration curve.

steps.title: Prepare spectrophotometric samples
steps.instruction: Derivatize the simulant extracts with Uranin and formaldehyde to form the MUF complex and measure absorbance.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 3.5 ml of the refrigerated simulant into a test tube.
Add 0.5 ml Uranin solution (6.3 µg ml⁻¹) and 1 ml formaldehyde.
Mix thoroughly to allow the Mannich reaction to proceed.
Place the tube in a spectrophotometer and scan from 200 nm to 400 nm to locate the maximum absorption (210 nm).
Prepare a blank containing all reagents except melamine; set its absorbance to zero.
Measure the absorbance of the sample at the identified maximum wavelength (210 nm).

steps.title: Calculate melamine migration from spectrophotometry
steps.instruction: Convert absorbance readings to melamine concentrations using the MUF calibration curve.

substeps.instruction: Insert each sample absorbance into the regression equation y = 0.0002x – 0.0045 (where y = absorbance, x = melamine concentration in µg ml⁻¹).
Apply the validation parameters (LOD, LOQ, accuracy, precision) to assess result reliability.
Report melamine migration in µg kg⁻¹ of food simulant (or ppb as appropriate).
